page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc5.6xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server from the High Clock Speed family, powered by the KVM hypervisor. The instance features 24 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs backed by Intel Xeon 6149 processors running at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz. System memory totals 48 GB, establishing a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio with 2.0 GB per core designed primarily for calculation-heavy tasks rather than large in-memory caching.

Storage and networking configurations reflect a stateless compute profile. The instance includes no local disk storage, requiring external cloud storage volumes for all persistent OS and data operations. Networking throughput is provisioned with a 4 Gbps baseline bandwidth, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are allocated by default. The absence of integrated local solid-state storage reduces idle disk costs and maintenance overhead, though persistent I/O performance relies on attached network storage.

Cost efficiency is optimized for compute-heavy workloads where processor frequency dictates execution runtime. By allocating a compact memory footprint relative to its 24 dedicated cores and excluding bundled local disks, infrastructure resources remain concentrated on raw execution capacity. The server fits workloads such as continuous integration build pipelines, distributed batch computation, application compilation, media encoding, and dedicated game servers.

The server delivers 24 dedicated vCPUs driven by an Intel Xeon 6149 processor clocked at 3.1 GHz, coupled with 48 GB of RAM at a 2.0 GB per core allocation. It is suitable for batch computing, compilation pipelines, video transcoding, and distributed mathematical processing.
